title: Her rooms on C deck (the shelter deck): R3, a sourced table of facts
written: 2026-11-20, by the R3 session (Claude Opus 5.5), under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md, on the coordinator's word after D deck and the orlop
rules: Facts only: which room, where, how big, which door to which. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites the reference read and the original checked, or says it was not checked. Bets are tagged as bets.
reference: ET: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, C deck (https://www.encyclopedia-titanica.org/titanic-deckplans/c-deck.html; drawn by Bruce Beveridge for Titanic The Ship Magnificent, The History Press 2008), read on the page in the built-in browser on 2026-11-20, nothing saved
original: Shipbuilder 1911: The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 (the Olympic and Titanic number), its plate of the shelter deck (C), as reproduced by GG Archives (https://www.ggarchives.com/OT/Titanic/25-ImageLibrary/TheShipbuilder-10-Design-SpecialPlates.html); too small to read room by room, not opened this time.
how: Walls by her frames. The plan's scale was found from its own frame ticks along the centreline (30.8 px a frame amidships: 0.0975 ft a pixel, E deck's scale), with the midship section between the ticks of 1A and 1F. A ruler of her frames (E deck's anchors) was drawn over the page at that scale; the plan's printed frame numbers at 140A, 1F and 140F fall on it within a few inches. Walls were read against the ruler at 1:1 or 3:4 (to about half a frame). The passages' walls, the poop front, the house's two ends and the forecastle's after wall were measured by pixel profiles of the page at 1:1 (to a pixel); those rows are tagged 'profiled'.
Frames to feet: E deck's anchors (data/rooms/E_deck.json), with C deck's own ends: the stern 455.5 ft abaft amidships (the plan's outer line on the centreline) and the stem 429.2 ft forward [approx].

y: feet from the centreline, port positive, at 0.0979 ft a pixel (the breadth over the shell amidships: 947 px for 92.67 ft, as on D deck). 'shell+' and 'shell-' are her side; in metres the tool puts it at the model's half-breadth halfway between C and B decks [stand-in for the reference's shell].

Block level: a row is a block of rooms between passages (its cabin numbers in plan), a public room, a casing, a stair or a crew space. The two well decks are open to the sky and have no rows; the forecastle and the poop over C deck are B-level weather decks.
No watertight bulkhead is marked on C deck by the reference; a thin line across the windlass room at about 138.5F is not marked watertight. The table's bulkheads is empty.

Doors: 2 ft 3 in by default [bet], unless the reference writes one (the second-class promenade's doors in her side: 6 ft 0 in by 4 ft 3 in clear opening). Stairs are listed among the doors with no width.
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, poly_m, area_m2, zone, slab, plan_compartment) are written by: node tools/rooms_table.js --write data/rooms/C_deck.json

frames.note: E deck's anchors (her frames, feet forward of amidships), with C deck's own stern and stem.

bulkheads.note: None: the reference marks no watertight bulkhead on C deck.

side.note: Read 2026-11-20 between 22:50 and 23:02 CST, both sides, with the line test. The first reading, about 21:25 (port only, the first dark pixel), is replaced: it agreed within 0.1 ft except at 120A, where an annotation gave 42.8 ft. For BACKLOG G14 (the hull's ends): tools/rooms_table_tests.js sets each against the model's half-breadth. Frames 75A to 40A and 40F to 75F added 2026-11-21 between 05:20 and 05:45 CST by the B1+B2 lane, the same method in the built-in browser (nothing saved), for C3 (the epoch's hull ends, D80; G20's G14 half): every 5 frames, no reading off the smooth line through its neighbours by more than 0.1 m, so no single frames were added. At R3's 80A and 80F on C and D decks, and at 80F and 80A on E, the same reading gives R3's figures within 0.1 ft (one pixel).
side.unit: ft from the centreline to her outer line as the plan draws it, port and starboard, read on the page at 1:1 by pixel profile: from her outside inward, the first dark pixel that lies on a continuous line (a dark path running at least 28 px each way along her), at three columns 6 px apart about the frame's tick; the median of the three. Annotations outside her (labels, dimension arrows) fail the line test. null: no reading (the line broken there by fittings).
